messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] A small note about the core mechanic to pass expressions in Rhipe
parts:
Sorry I don't mean to upset you!

I do have an idea though.  I was playing around with the serialization object like so:

 s = testSerialize3()
> rawToChar(serialize(unserialize(charToRaw(s)), NULL, ascii=TRUE))

That tells you that even though it unserializes to the same expression it has data with the expression that is not the same.  "str" doesn't show it.  Neither does attributes while it is on the expression itself, but if you attributes the first element of a expression you start to get somewhere:

For example,
testExpr = function() expression({test})
 attributes(testExpr()[[1]])
$srcref[[1]]
{

$srcref[[2]]
test


$srcfile
 

$wholeSrcref
testExpr = function() expression({test}



Basically the attributes need to be stripped, but the expression object has elements and they need to be stripped in that.

A little demo:

 testSerialize4 = function()  {

attributes(expr[[1]]) = NULL
rawToChar(serialize(expr, NULL, ascii=TRUE))
}


> testSerialize4()
[1] "A 2 196608 131840 20 1 6 1 262153 1 { 2 1 262153 4 test 254 "
> unserialize(charToRaw(testSerialize4()))
expression({
    test
})


You can see that testSerialize4() has been spared testSerialize3() fate.

Now all this said.  Idea hasn't been tested in MapReduce and I believe the multiple expression format of Reduce will require a closer inspection and perhaps several nullings.  Right now it is a user-level idea to deal with this reality.

Thanks

On Tue, May 7, 2013 at 12:27 PM, Jeremiah Rounds <roundsj...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,  I was debugging some code for a colleague and I happened to inspect the serializations for MapReduce expressions that appear in lines of Rhipe:::.rhmr


I noticed that  serialize(expr, NULL, ascii=TRUE) creates an arbitrarily large string for fixed expr.  The length of string depends on the containing environment, so that if expressions are created in very large functions they generate very large serializations.  

For example consider these cases and the resulting serialization:

# Version 1 #
 testSerialize = function(){ expr = expression({test}); rawToChar(serialize(expr, NULL, ascii=TRUE))}
> testSerialize()
[1] "A 2 196608 131840 20 1 518 1026 1 262153 6 srcref 19 2 781 8 1 47 1 47 47 47 1 1 1026 1 262153 7 srcfile 4 0 242 1026 1 262153 5 lines 16 1 262153 101 testSerialize\040=\040function(){\040expr\040=\040expression({test});\040rawToChar(serialize(expr,\040NULL,\040ascii=TRUE))}\n 1026 1 262153 8 filename 16 1 262153 0 254 254 1026 1 262153 5 class 16 2 262153 11 srcfilecopy 262153 7 srcfile 254 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 781 8 1 48 1 51 48 51 1 1 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 1026 767 1023 1026 1 262153 11 wholeSrcref 781 8 1 0 1 52 0 52 1 1 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 254 1 262153 1 { 2 1 262153 4 test 254 "


# Version 2 #
testSerialize2 = function(expr) rawToChar(serialize(expr, NULL, ascii=TRUE))
> testSerialize2(expression({test}))
[1] "A 2 196608 131840 20 1 518 1026 1 262153 6 srcref 19 2 781 8 1 27 1 27 27 27 1 1 1026 1 262153 7 srcfile 4 0 242 1026 1 262153 5 lines 16 1 262153 35 testSerialize2(expression({test}))\n 1026 1 262153 8 filename 16 1 262153 0 254 254 1026 1 262153 5 class 16 2 262153 11 srcfilecopy 262153 7 srcfile 254 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 781 8 1 28 1 31 28 31 1 1 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 1026 767 1023 1026 1 262153 11 wholeSrcref 781 8 1 0 1 32 0 32 1 1 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 254 1 262153 1 { 2 1 262153 4 test 254 "


#Version 3 #

> rawToChar(serialize(expression({test}), NULL, ascii=TRUE))
[1] "A 2 196608 131840 20 1 518 1026 1 262153 6 srcref 19 2 781 8 1 32 1 32 32 32 1 1 1026 1 262153 7 srcfile 4 0 242 1026 1 262153 5 lines 16 1 262153 59 rawToChar(serialize(expression({test}),\040NULL,\040ascii=TRUE))\n 1026 1 262153 8 filename 16 1 262153 0 254 254 1026 1 262153 5 class 16 2 262153 11 srcfilecopy 262153 7 srcfile 254 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 781 8 1 33 1 36 33 36 1 1 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 1026 767 1023 1026 1 262153 11 wholeSrcref 781 8 1 0 1 37 0 37 1 1 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 254 1 262153 1 { 2 1 262153 4 test 254 "


They all unserialize to:  

expression({
    test
})

But, 
Version 1 contains the entire contents of the function "testSerialize"
Version 2 contains the entire call to the function "testSerialize2"
Version 3 contains just the serialization command.


To show you why this can be bad

 testSerialize3 = function()  {
#########################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################
expr = expression({test}); 
rawToChar(serialize(expr, NULL, ascii=TRUE))
}
> testSerialize3()
[1] "A 2 196608 131840 20 1 518 1026 1 262153 6 srcref 19 2 781 8 3 19 3 19 19 19 3 3 1026 1 262153 7 srcfile 4 0 242 1026 1 262153 5 lines 16 1 262153 1045 \040testSerialize3\040=\040function()\040\040{\n#########################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################################\nexpr\040=\040expression({test});\040\nrawToChar(serialize(expr,\040NULL,\040ascii=TRUE))\n}\n 1026 1 262153 8 filename 16 1 262153 0 254 254 1026 1 262153 5 class 16 2 262153 11 srcfilecopy 262153 7 srcfile 254 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 781 8 3 20 3 23 20 23 3 3 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 1026 767 1023 1026 1 262153 11 wholeSrcref 781 8 1 0 3 24 0 24 1 3 1026 767 1023 1026 1791 16 1 262153 6 srcref 254 254 1 262153 1 { 2 1 262153 4 test 254 "


Superfluous junk that had nothing to do with expr is carried along making how long string serializations passed through to Java have a length depending where the reduce or map was created.

To get rid of my colleagues error this worked for me (embedded in a much larger function).  I am not actually sure why yet.  The first sign of the error was in the Mapper ProcessBuilder having an error in starting the runner, but the error didn't exist if we removed the rhwatch from inside a large function, and it goes away with stripping attributes on the map and reduce (which were very large).

nullAttributes = function(e){ for(i in seq_along(e)) attributes(e[[i]]) = NULL; return(e)} 
map = nullAttributes(map)  #map came from rhmap but this still works.
reduce = nullAttributes(reduce)
      tmp <- rhwatch(
         map=map, 
         reduce=reduce, 
         input=rhfmt(obj$loc, type=obj$type), 
         mapred=mapred, 
         readback=TRUE, 
         parameters=list(needs = needList, trans=obj$trans)
      )

parts:
is the R not starting? Then this because the expression/function has tons of environmental attributes which blow it up.
And then these are passed in environmental variables.

The solution? Add these to the param file - setup/map/reduce/cleanup. But that needs some C side engineering.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] A small note about the core mechanic to pass expressions in Rhipe
parts:
It was for datadr.  The R interpreter was not starting for one of the clusters it was being tested on.  I didn't record the exact error but it was 127 with a complaint about parameters in the ProcessBuilder.  I ended up placing a wrapper for rhwatch in the datadr namespace like what follows that seemed to solve the problem.  It perhaps could be interpreted as an increase in robustness for Rhipe.


rhwatch = function(map = NULL, reduce=NULL, combiner=FALSE, setup=NULL, ...){
#cat("In datadr namespace rhwatch\n")

nullAttributes = function(e) { 
for(i in seq_along(e)) attributes(e[[i]]) = NULL
return(e)
}

if(!is.null(map)) map = nullAttributes(map)
if(!is.null(reduce)) reduce = nullAttributes(reduce)
if(!is.null(setup)) setup = nullAttributes(setup)
Rhipe:::rhwatch(map,reduce,combiner, setup,...)

}

parts:
good, but it is a temporary fix. Ideally you dont want to remove attributes from functions - not RHIPE's job (unless is causing things to crash, e.g. remove the Rhipe namespace is important).
Hence placing them in the param Rdata (which is loaded in setup) is the right way to go.
